ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure there are four AC waveforms, labeled respectively as (a), (b), (c), and (d). Figure (a) crosses zero at 0, π, and 2π; from 0 to π it is the positive half-cycle, and from π to 2π it is the negative half-cycle. Figure (b) has a phase shift relative to the origin, and its zero-crossing positions do not completely coincide with figure (a). Figure (c) also has a phase shift, and the waveform zero crossings are not completely consistent with figure (a). Figure (d) has the same or corresponding zero-crossing positions as figure (a), crossing zero at 0, π, and 2π, but from 0 to π it is the negative half-cycle, and from π to 2π it is the positive half-cycle. Reasoning: According to the draft method, taking figure (a) as the reference, an anticorrelated or antiphase waveform should have the same zero-crossing times, but the signs at any corresponding time are opposite. Figure (d) exactly satisfies this: when figure (a) is positive, figure (d) is negative; when figure (a) is negative, figure (d) is positive. Therefore the ones showing an anticorrelation relationship are figure (a) and figure (d).

raw_record.question_text: Through the oscilloscope, the following AC waveforms are observed. Which two figures show an inverse relationship?

method.method_draft: First inspect each plotted AC waveform and compare their time positions. Use figure (a) as a reference: it crosses zero at 0, π, and 2π, with a positive half-cycle from 0 to π and a negative half-cycle from π to 2π. Then look for another figure with the same zero-crossing positions but opposite sign throughout. Figure (d) has matching zero crossings but its first half-cycle is negative and its second half-cycle is positive, so it is the inverted version of (a). Therefore the two figures showing an inverse relationship are Figure (a) and Figure (d).

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Direct phase-comparison route: it identifies inverse relationship by matching zero crossings and extrema with opposite signs, rather than using labels or circuit context.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the four oscilloscope sketches labeled (a)–(d). Note that (a) starts at zero and rises positive, crosses zero near π, reaches a negative half-cycle before 2π; (d) starts at zero but immediately goes negative, crosses zero near π, then reaches a positive half-cycle before 2π. The other figures include phase shifts marked φ or do not align as exact opposites of (a).
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question statement to determine the task: select which two of the displayed AC waveforms have an inverse relationship.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: For sinusoidal AC waveforms, an inverse relationship means one waveform is the negative of the other at every corresponding time, equivalently a 180° or π rad phase difference: when one has a positive peak the other has a negative peak, and their zero crossings occur at the same times.
